Page 14, last paragraph. The dust problem is especially bad in the desert and should be mentioned in this statement.
Page 15, last paragraph. The California Department of Fish and Game has set up quali guzzlers in many areas of the California desert and some game birds are entirely dependent on this source of water. Cross country motorcycle races have been routed right by some of these. Vandalism in areas accessible only by ORVs has also been a critical problem with quali guzzlers.
The Desert Bighorn Sheep is known to disappear in areas of heavy human use.

This species should receive a higher priority in management decisions than ORVs.
Page 16, paragraph 2. It should be emphasized here that ORV use should be considered harmful to wildlife until proven otherwise. All areas should be considered closed until it is shown that ORVs would have an acceptable impact upon wildlife.
Page 16, paragraph 3. The only ORV users who might need access to game management purposes are the game and land managers themselves. If it is determined that an area should be closed to ORVs, then hunters should walk or ride horses. It should be very clear that an area normally closed to ORVs will not be opened to hunters on ORVs merely because of a surplus of game.
Page 17, line 11. This mentions revenues from sales of motorcycles. It should be recognized that not all motorcycles are used as ORVs. Only those that are used as ORVs should be included in the statement.
Page 17, lines 15-16. Winter access to small towns via snowmobiles can be on snow covered roads and need not be cross country.
Page 18, line 11. The case for strengthened family relationships caused by ORV use should be proven. Saying there is reason to believe this is true is not enough. The reasons should be spelled out.
